{"parentUuid":"20124825-6932-4f45-b6bc-2b44f2360beb","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"07d5b485-40a3-4b47-9abd-8fd6f4b942c2","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01S8DgXdYjVVZnQbGVVEV9gS","type":"tool_result","content":"## Parent\n\nPart of #11\n\n## What to build\n\nA Data Bite can carry chart images (PNG, JPEG, WebP), uploaded and deleted on its edit page, and shown inline wherever its Markdown body references them as `image:<name>`: the admin preview, its public page, and the `cms publish` export. This ticket builds the shared image code (validation, storage, the `image:` rewrite in the Markdown pipeline, the public and export paths) that T11 reuses for Reports.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Any Analyst or the Director can upload an image to any Data Bite, draft or published; the edit page lists its images, each with a copyable `![Description](image:<name>)` snippet\n- [ ] Only real PNG, JPEG, or WebP files are accepted, checked by content with the extension and declared type agreeing; SVG is rejected; the filename is sanitized before use in any path\n- [ ] Images over 5 MB, or beyond 10 on one Data Bite, are rejected with a clear error\n- [ ] Uploading a name the Data Bite already has replaces that image; an image can be deleted\n- [ ] `image:<name>` renders as an `<img>` with the right `src` and the Markdown description as `alt`, in the preview, on the public page, and in the export; an unknown name renders nothing\n- [ ] The edit page warns, without blocking the save, when an `image:` reference has an empty description\n- [ ] A published Data Bite's images are served at `images/data-bites/<slug>/<name>` and exported there with relative paths; a draft's never are, and unpublishing takes them down\n- [ ] Deleting a Data Bite deletes its images\n- [ ] Every image route requires login, carries CSRF on its forms, and rejects a CSRF-stripped post\n- [ ] Tests cover all of the above, including that the export stays identical to the live site (T08)\n\n## Blocked by\n\nNone. Can start immediately.\n\n[\"ticket\"]\n-----\n# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. This ticket builds the shared image code (validation, storage, the `image:` rewrite in the Markdown pipeline, the public and export paths) that T11 reuses for Reports.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Any Analyst or the Director can upload an image to any Data Bite, draft or published; the edit page lists its images, each with a copyable `![Description](image:<name>)` snippet\n- [ ] Only real PNG, JPEG, or WebP files are accepted, checked by content with the extension and declared type agreeing; SVG is rejected; the filename is sanitized before use in any path\n- [ ] Images over 5 MB, or beyond 10 on one Data Bite, are rejected with a clear error\n- [ ] Uploading a name the Data Bite already has replaces that image; an image can be deleted\n- [ ] `image:<name>` renders as an `<img>` with the right `src` and the Markdown description as `alt`, in the preview, on the public page, and in the export; an unknown name renders nothing\n- [ ] The edit page warns, without blocking the save, when an `image:` reference has an empty description\n- [ ] A published Data Bite's images are served at `images/data-bites/<slug>/<name>` and exported there with relative paths; a draft's never are, and unpublishing takes them down\n- [ ] Deleting a Data Bite deletes its images\n- [ ] Every image route requires login, carries CSRF on its forms, and rejects a CSRF-stripped post\n- [ ] Tests cover all of the above, including that the export stays identical to the live site (T08)\n\n## Blocked by\n\nNone. {"parentUuid":"03095982-3c7d-4b3d-b923-976ad88fb421","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaAbbebFDwYoLLtiyJFd","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_011Z8SeaqPSbwXB9LzQgdPan","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc/scratchpad/spec-editor.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nThe office's writers are IR staff and interns, not web developers, but every Data Bite and Report body is typed as Markdown in a plain textarea. A table means lining up pipes by hand, a chart means making it in Excel, exporting a PNG, uploading it, and typing `image:<name>`, and a link to the Factbook means pasting a URL that breaks if the site moves. The preview under the textarea uses the admin console's styling, so nobody sees the page as a visitor will until after `cms publish`.\n\nGoal: turn the CMS from a Markdown publishing tool into a document-style authoring environment. Nontechnical staff can write, paste, build tables and charts, and preview the exact public result without ever seeing the underlying content format.\n\n## Solution\n\n- The **Editor**, a hand-built visual editor, replaces the Markdown textarea. It has a toolbar, cleans up pasted text, and turns a range pasted from Excel or Sheets into a table. The body is still **stored as Markdown**, so the sanitizer, `cms publish`, and existing content are unchanged (ADR-005).\n- Tables are built and edited in place.\n- A **Chart** is built from data typed or pasted into the CMS and drawn by the server as inline SVG, with its data available as a table (ADR-006, which reverses ADR-004's deferral). Uploaded **Chart images** stay and get an \"Insert image\" button.\n- Links to other Reports and Data Bites are picked from a list and stored by id, so they stay correct when slugs or the site's address change.\n- A **Site preview** shows the draft as the public page (site nav, stylesheet, date line) beside the Editor and in a new tab, with a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner.\n\nControls are functional and minimally styled. A visual design pass for the admin console comes later, in its own spec.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an Analyst, I want to write a Data Bite with toolbar buttons for bold, italic, lists, headings, and quotes, so that I never have to learn Markdown.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to paste text from Word or Google Docs and keep its bold, lists, headings, and links but not its fonts or colours, so that pasted content matches the site.\n3. As an Analyst, I want to paste a range from Excel or Sheets and get a table, so that I don't retype numbers.\n4. As an Analyst, I want to edit a table in place and add or remove rows and columns, so that fixing a number takes one click.\n5. As a visitor, I want numeric table columns right-aligned, so that figures line up and compare easily.\n6. As an Analyst, I want to build a bar or line chart by typing or pasting data, and see it drawn as I go, so that a survey result gets a chart without Excel exports.\n7. As an Analyst, I want a clear message next to a cell the chart can't read, so that I know exactly what to fix.\n8. As an Analyst, I want suppressed values (`*`, `<10`) to be accepted and marked as suppressed, so that a chart respects small-cell privacy rules.\n9. As a visitor using a screen reader, I want each Chart named by its title and its data available as a table, so that I get the numbers without seeing the chart.\n10. As an Analyst, I want to link to another Report or Data Bite by picking it from a list, so that the link survives slug changes and the site moving.\n11. As a visitor, I want a link to an item that isn't published to show as plain text, not a broken link.\n12. As a Director, I want to be told which items link to an item before I delete it, so that I know which pages will lose a link.\n13. As an Analyst, I want to insert an uploaded Chart image with a button that requires a description, so that I can't forget the alt text.\n14. As an Analyst or Director, I want to see the draft exactly as the public page will look, at desktop and phone widths, so that I catch problems before publishing.\n15. As an Analyst or Director, I want a warning before I leave a page with unsaved changes, so that I don't lose work.\n16. As a Director, I want opening and saving an untouched item to leave its stored body byte-for-byte unchanged, so that the Editor never rewrites content nobody edited.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Editor and storage (T13, ADR-005)\n\n- **No dependency.** The Editor is `contenteditable` plus a toolbar in vanilla JS with no build step (ADR-002). It supports current Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.\n- **Markdown stays the storage format.** On load, the server renders the body to Editor HTML with the existing pipeline. On save, the Editor posts its HTML, and the server sanitizes it with nh3 and converts it to Markdown with stdlib `html.parser` (a new module, testable with pytest).\n- **Toolbar:** bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, link, Section (H2), Subsection (H3), block quote. The title stays the only H1. There's no underline, font, colour, or alignment, because Markdown can't hold them.\n- **Untouched is byte-for-byte:** if the writer changes nothing, the stored Markdown is kept exactly, and opening the Editor never rewrites it.\n- **An edited body is saved in standard Markdown form:** any body the Editor has changed is rewritten in one standard form.\n- **Locked blocks:** a block the Editor can't represent (code block, raw HTML, H4 or deeper, etc.) shows as a read-only block reading \"This part can't be edited here\". Its original Markdown is kept byte-for-byte even when blocks around it are edited. No current content triggers this.\n- **Paste:** only supported formatting survives. An HTML table on the clipboard (from Excel or Sheets) becomes an Editor table. A pasted or dropped picture is refused with a message pointing to \"Insert image\" (T18).\n- **Unsaved changes:** a `beforeunload` warning is shown when the Editor is dirty. There's no autosave, since that would publish half-finished text on a published Data Bite.\n- **Fallback:** the Editor takes over the existing `body` textarea. If the script fails, the textarea still works and posts Markdown as it does today.\n\n### Links (T14)\n\n- External links are limited to `https:` and `mailto:`. Anything else, including `javascript:`, root-absolute `/…`, and `http:`, is refused with a message in the link dialog and removed by the server on save.\n- **Links within the site** are stored as `report:<id>` or `data-bite:<id>`, by the stable database id and never by title or slug. The Markdown pipeline resolves them at render time to the page-relative path, like `image:<name>` (ADR-004).\n- A target that's a draft, unpublished, deleted, or missing renders as **plain text** (its link text, with no `<a>`), never as an empty or unsafe link. The reference stays stored, so it becomes a link again if the target is published.\n- In the Editor, such links are marked \"Not published: will show as plain text\" or \"Item deleted\".\n- Deleting an item shows the items whose bodies link to it, and the delete isn't blocked.\n- `cms publish` regenerates all of `site/` on every run (`app/publish.py`), so a link becomes live on the first publish after its target is published. No pages need rebuilding individually.\n\n### Tables (T15)\n\n- Edited in place in the Editor, with add/remove row and column controls shown while the cursor is in a table. Stored as a Markdown table (T09 styling and scroll wrapper unchanged).\n- The first row is always the header.\n- **Right-aligned automatically** when every non-empty cell in a column is numeric. Numeric means digits with optional thousands commas, a leading `-` or `$`, a trailing `%`, or accounting parentheses `(3.2)`. Blank, `—`, and `n/a` cells don't stop a column counting as numeric.\n\n### Charts (T16 rendering, ADR-006; T17 builder)\n\n- **Stored** as a fenced `chart` block in the Markdown body, holding the type, title, axis labels, units, source, and data. Writers never see it.\n- **Types:** vertical bar, horizontal bar, line. 1 to 4 series, with a legend when there's more than one. Up to 30 categories for bar charts and 60 for line charts.\n- **Fields:** title (required), x- and y-axis labels (optional), Units (optional), Source/note (optional; one line of plain text with no formatting).\n- **Palette:** fixed and accessible, and writers can't choose colours.\n- **Number parsing:** a value may have thousands commas, a leading `-`, accounting parentheses (negative), a trailing `%`, or a leading `$`. Any other currency symbol is an inline error.\n- **Units:** `$` is a unit *prefix* and `%` a unit *suffix*, and the chart stores which one it is. Units typed as a word (\"students\") is a suffix, with a space before it. One chart has one unit, and mixing `$` and `%` is an inline error naming the first conflicting cell. A `%` in the data sets the units to `%` if none are given.\n- **Missing values:** blank, `—`, `n/a`. A table means lining up pipes by hand, a chart means making it in Excel, exporting a PNG, uploading it, and typing `image:<name>`, and a link to the Factbook means pasting a URL that breaks if the site moves. The preview under the textarea uses the admin console's styling, so nobody sees the page as a visitor will until after `cms publish`.\n\nGoal: turn the CMS from a Markdown publishing tool into a document-style authoring environment. Nontechnical staff can write, paste, build tables and charts, and preview the exact public result without ever seeing the underlying content format.\n\n## Solution\n\n- The **Editor**, a hand-built visual editor, replaces the Markdown textarea. It has a toolbar, cleans up pasted text, and turns a range pasted from Excel or Sheets into a table. The body is still **stored as Markdown**, so the sanitizer, `cms publish`, and existing content are unchanged (ADR-005).\n- Tables are built and edited in place.\n- A **Chart** is built from data typed or pasted into the CMS and drawn by the server as inline SVG, with its data available as a table (ADR-006, which reverses ADR-004's deferral). Uploaded **Chart images** stay and get an \"Insert image\" button.\n- Links to other Reports and Data Bites are picked from a list and stored by id, so they stay correct when slugs or the site's address change.\n- A **Site preview** shows the draft as the public page (site nav, stylesheet, date line) beside the Editor and in a new tab, with a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner.\n\nControls are functional and minimally styled. A visual design pass for the admin console comes later, in its own spec.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As an Analyst, I want to write a Data Bite with toolbar buttons for bold, italic, lists, headings, and quotes, so that I never have to learn Markdown.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to paste text from Word or Google Docs and keep its bold, lists, headings, and links but not its fonts or colours, so that pasted content matches the site.\n3. As an Analyst, I want to paste a range from Excel or Sheets and get a table, so that I don't retype numbers.\n4. As an Analyst, I want to edit a table in place and add or remove rows and columns, so that fixing a number takes one click.\n5. As a visitor, I want numeric table columns right-aligned, so that figures line up and compare easily.\n6. As an Analyst, I want to build a bar or line chart by typing or pasting data, and see it drawn as I go, so that a survey result gets a chart without Excel exports.\n7. As an Analyst, I want a clear message next to a cell the chart can't read, so that I know exactly what to fix.\n8. As an Analyst, I want suppressed values (`*`, `<10`) to be accepted and marked as suppressed, so that a chart respects small-cell privacy rules.\n9. As a visitor using a screen reader, I want each Chart named by its title and its data available as a table, so that I get the numbers without seeing the chart.\n10. As an Analyst, I want to link to another Report or Data Bite by picking it from a list, so that the link survives slug changes and the site moving.\n11. As a visitor, I want a link to an item that isn't published to show as plain text, not a broken link.\n12. As a Director, I want to be told which items link to an item before I delete it, so that I know which pages will lose a link.\n13. As an Analyst, I want to insert an uploaded Chart image with a button that requires a description, so that I can't forget the alt text.\n14. As an Analyst or Director, I want to see the draft exactly as the public page will look, at desktop and phone widths, so that I catch problems before publishing.\n15. As an Analyst or Director, I want a warning before I leave a page with unsaved changes, so that I don't lose work.\n16. As a Director, I want opening and saving an untouched item to leave its stored body byte-for-byte unchanged, so that the Editor never rewrites content nobody edited.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Editor and storage (T13, ADR-005)\n\n- **No dependency.** The Editor is `contenteditable` plus a toolbar in vanilla JS with no build step (ADR-002). It supports current Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.\n- **Markdown stays the storage format.** On load, the server renders the body to Editor HTML with the existing pipeline. On save, the Editor posts its HTML, and the server sanitizes it with nh3 and converts it to Markdown with stdlib `html.parser` (a new module, testable with pytest).\n- **Toolbar:** bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, link, Section (H2), Subsection (H3), block quote. The title stays the only H1. There's no underline, font, colour, or alignment, because Markdown can't hold them.\n- **Untouched is byte-for-byte:** if the writer changes nothing, the stored Markdown is kept exactly, and opening the Editor never rewrites it.\n- **An edited body is saved in standard Markdown form:** any body the Editor has changed is rewritten in one standard form.\n- **Locked blocks:** a block the Editor can't represent (code block, raw HTML, H4 or deeper, etc.) shows as a read-only block reading \"This part can't be edited here\". Its original Markdown is kept byte-for-byte even when blocks around it are edited. No current content triggers this.\n- **Paste:** only supported formatting survives. An HTML table on the clipboard (from Excel or Sheets) becomes an Editor table. A pasted or dropped picture is refused with a message pointing to \"Insert image\" (T18).\n- **Unsaved changes:** a `beforeunload` warning is shown when the Editor is dirty. There's no autosave, since that would publish half-finished text on a published Data Bite.\n- **Fallback:** the Editor takes over the existing `body` textarea. If the script fails, the textarea still works and posts Markdown as it does today.\n\n### Links (T14)\n\n- External links are limited to `https:` and `mailto:`. Anything else, including `javascript:`, root-absolute `/…`, and `http:`, is refused with a message in the link dialog and removed by the server on save.\n- **Links within the site** are stored as `report:<id>` or `data-bite:<id>`, by the stable database id and never by title or slug. The Markdown pipeline resolves them at render time to the page-relative path, like `image:<name>` (ADR-004).\n- A target that's a draft, unpublished, deleted, or missing renders as **plain text** (its link text, with no `<a>`), never as an empty or unsafe link. The reference stays stored, so it becomes a link again if the target is published.\n- In the Editor, such links are marked \"Not published: will show as plain text\" or \"Item deleted\".\n- Deleting an item shows the items whose bodies link to it, and the delete isn't blocked.\n- `cms publish` regenerates all of `site/` on every run (`app/publish.py`), so a link becomes live on the first publish after its target is published. No pages need rebuilding individually.\n\n### Tables (T15)\n\n- Edited in place in the Editor, with add/remove row and column controls shown while the cursor is in a table. Stored as a Markdown table (T09 styling and scroll wrapper unchanged).\n- The first row is always the header.\n- **Right-aligned automatically** when every non-empty cell in a column is numeric. Numeric means digits with optional thousands commas, a leading `-` or `$`, a trailing `%`, or accounting parentheses `(3.2)`. Blank, `—`, and `n/a` cells don't stop a column counting as numeric.\n\n### Charts (T16 rendering, ADR-006; T17 builder)\n\n- **Stored** as a fenced `chart` block in the Markdown body, holding the type, title, axis labels, units, source, and data. Writers never see it.\n- **Types:** vertical bar, horizontal bar, line. 1 to 4 series, with a legend when there's more than one. Up to 30 categories for bar charts and 60 for line charts.\n- **Fields:** title (required), x- and y-axis labels (optional), Units (optional), Source/note (optional; one line of plain text with no formatting).\n- **Palette:** fixed and accessible, and writers can't choose colours.\n- **Number parsing:** a value may have thousands commas, a leading `-`, accounting parentheses (negative), a trailing `%`, or a leading `$`. Any other currency symbol is an inline error.\n- **Units:** `$` is a unit *prefix* and `%` a unit *suffix*, and the chart stores which one it is. Units typed as a word (\"students\") is a suffix, with a space before it. One chart has one unit, and mixing `$` and `%` is an inline error naming the first conflicting cell. A `%` in the data sets the units to `%` if none are given.\n- **Missing values:** blank, `—`, `n/a`. No bar is drawn, and a line shows a gap.\n- **Suppressed values:** the whole trimmed cell must match `*`, `<N`, `≤N`, or `<=N` (N a whole number).\n  - No mark is drawn.\n  - The data table keeps the original notation.\n  - \"Some values are suppressed for privacy\" appears once under the chart.\n- **Axes:** a bar chart always starts at zero. A line chart may start above zero and says so when it does. Values are labelled as typed, not re-rounded.\n- **Suggested type:** a long category label suggests horizontal bar but doesn't force it.\n- **Accessibility:** the SVG has `role=\"img\"` and the chart title as its accessible name. Under it, a `<details>` \"Show the data\" table is generated from the same data. The public site gets no JavaScript.\n- **Trusted SVG:** the chart block is replaced by a placeholder before nh3 runs, and the server-drawn SVG is swapped in after sanitizing. Every writer-typed string (title, labels, units, source, category and series names, cell text) is escaped before it goes into the SVG or the table. No uploaded SVG is ever served (ADR-004 unchanged).\n- **Builder (T17):** a dialog with a grid (categories down, series across) that accepts typing and an Excel or Sheets paste. It draws the chart live using the same server rendering, shows errors next to the cells, and has the Units field. In the body, a Chart is a card showing the drawn chart, with Edit and Remove.\n\n### Chart images in the Editor (T18)\n\n- \"Insert image\" lists the item's uploaded Chart images, and a description (alt) is required before inserting. It's stored as `![Description](image:<name>)` as today, and the existing upload, validation, and permissions (ADR-004) are unchanged.\n\n### Site preview (T12)\n\n- The draft is rendered through the public templates, `public_site.CSS`, and the site nav, with the item shown **as if published**: a draft Report appears in the nav. Other drafts stay hidden.\n- It's an embedded frame beside the Editor that drops below it on narrow screens, and it updates as the writer types (debounced, as today).\n- A Desktop/Phone width toggle.\n- \"Preview on site\" opens the same rendering in a new tab, showing the current **unsaved** edits (the form is posted to the tab, and nothing is saved).\n- A \"Draft preview, not published\" banner on every Site preview.\n- Preview routes require login and CSRF, save nothing, and follow the item's permissions (ADR-003).\n\n### Vocabulary\n\n- CONTEXT.md gains **Chart**, **Site preview**, and **Editor**, and **Chart image** is clarified as uploaded.\n- Avoid: graph, WYSIWYG, rich text, live view.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Behaviour is tested through `TestClient` with the `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures, as in #1 and #11. The pure modules (HTML → Markdown conversion, chart parsing, SVG drawing) also get direct pytest tests.\n- **Round trip:**\n  - An untouched body posted back is stored byte-for-byte.\n  - A no-change round trip through the standard form renders equivalent HTML, for every seed body and every T09/T10 test fixture.\n  - An edit to one block changes only that block's rendered HTML.\n  - A locked block's bytes survive edits to the blocks around it.\n- **Sanitizing:** Editor HTML carrying `<script>`, `onerror=`, `style=`, `javascript:` hrefs, root-absolute hrefs, and unknown tags is stored as safe Markdown, with none of it surviving to any render.\n- **Links:**\n  - A `report:<id>` or `data-bite:<id>` link renders a correct relative href on the public page, in the export, and in the Site preview.\n  - A draft, unpublished, deleted, or unknown target renders plain text with no `<a>`.\n  - Publishing the target and re-running the export turns it into a link.\n- **Tables:** Excel-style HTML becomes a Markdown table. Numeric-column detection works across the formats listed above.\n- **Charts:**\n  - Parsing is tested for every numeric, missing, suppressed, currency, and unit-conflict case.\n  - The SVG is well-formed, escapes hostile titles, labels, and cells, and gives bar charts a zero baseline.\n  - \"Show the data\" preserves the original notation.\n  - The privacy note appears exactly once.\n  - Category limits are enforced.\n- **Site preview:** a draft's Site preview shows the banner and uses the public stylesheet. As an Analyst, I want to link to another Report or Data Bite by picking it from a list, so that the link survives slug changes and the site moving.\n11. As a visitor, I want a link to an item that isn't published to show as plain text, not a broken link.\n12. As a Director, I want to be told which items link to an item before I delete it, so that I know which pages will lose a link.\n13. As an Analyst, I want to insert an uploaded Chart image with a button that requires a description, so that I can't forget the alt text.\n14. As an Analyst or Director, I want to see the draft exactly as the public page will look, at desktop and phone widths, so that I catch problems before publishing.\n15. As an Analyst or Director, I want a warning before I leave a page with unsaved changes, so that I don't lose work.\n16. As a Director, I want opening and saving an untouched item to leave its stored body byte-for-byte unchanged, so that the Editor never rewrites content nobody edited.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Editor and storage (T13, ADR-005)\n\n- **No dependency.** The Editor is `contenteditable` plus a toolbar in vanilla JS with no build step (ADR-002). It supports current Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.\n- **Markdown stays the storage format.** On load, the server renders the body to Editor HTML with the existing pipeline. On save, the Editor posts its HTML, and the server sanitizes it with nh3 and converts it to Markdown with stdlib `html.parser` (a new module, testable with pytest).\n- **Toolbar:** bold, italic, bulleted list, numbered list, link, Section (H2), Subsection (H3), block quote. The title stays the only H1. There's no underline, font, colour, or alignment, because Markdown can't hold them.\n- **Untouched is byte-for-byte:** if the writer changes nothing, the stored Markdown is kept exactly, and opening the Editor never rewrites it.\n- **An edited body is saved in standard Markdown form:** any body the Editor has changed is rewritten in one standard form.\n- **Locked blocks:** a block the Editor can't represent (code block, raw HTML, H4 or deeper, etc.) shows as a read-only block reading \"This part can't be edited here\". Its original Markdown is kept byte-for-byte even when blocks around it are edited. No current content triggers this.\n- **Paste:** only supported formatting survives. An HTML table on the clipboard (from Excel or Sheets) becomes an Editor table. A pasted or dropped picture is refused with a message pointing to \"Insert image\" (T18).\n- **Unsaved changes:** a `beforeunload` warning is shown when the Editor is dirty. There's no autosave, since that would publish half-finished text on a published Data Bite.\n- **Fallback:** the Editor takes over the existing `body` textarea. If the script fails, the textarea still works and posts Markdown as it does today.\n\n### Links (T14)\n\n- External links are limited to `https:` and `mailto:`. Anything else, including `javascript:`, root-absolute `/…`, and `http:`, is refused with a message in the link dialog and removed by the server on save.\n- **Links within the site** are stored as `report:<id>` or `data-bite:<id>`, by the stable database id and never by title or slug. The Markdown pipeline resolves them at render time to the page-relative path, like `image:<name>` (ADR-004).\n- A target that's a draft, unpublished, deleted, or missing renders as **plain text** (its link text, with no `<a>`), never as an empty or unsafe link. The reference stays stored, so it becomes a link again if the target is published.\n- In the Editor, such links are marked \"Not published: will show as plain text\" or \"Item deleted\".\n- Deleting an item shows the items whose bodies link to it, and the delete isn't blocked.\n- `cms publish` regenerates all of `site/` on every run (`app/publish.py`), so a link becomes live on the first publish after its target is published. No pages need rebuilding individually.\n\n### Tables (T15)\n\n- Edited in place in the Editor, with add/remove row and column controls shown while the cursor is in a table. Stored as a Markdown table (T09 styling and scroll wrapper unchanged).\n- The first row is always the header.\n- **Right-aligned automatically** when every non-empty cell in a column is numeric. Numeric means digits with optional thousands commas, a leading `-` or `$`, a trailing `%`, or accounting parentheses `(3.2)`. Blank, `—`, and `n/a` cells don't stop a column counting as numeric.\n\n### Charts (T16 rendering, ADR-006; T17 builder)\n\n- **Stored** as a fenced `chart` block in the Markdown body, holding the type, title, axis labels, units, source, and data. Writers never see it.\n- **Types:** vertical bar, horizontal bar, line. 1 to 4 series, with a legend when there's more than one. Up to 30 categories for bar charts and 60 for line charts.\n- **Fields:** title (required), x- and y-axis labels (optional), Units (optional), Source/note (optional; one line of plain text with no formatting).\n- **Palette:** fixed and accessible, and writers can't choose colours.\n- **Number parsing:** a value may have thousands commas, a leading `-`, accounting parentheses (negative), a trailing `%`, or a leading `$`. Any other currency symbol is an inline error.\n- **Units:** `$` is a unit *prefix* and `%` a unit *suffix*, and the chart stores which one it is. Units typed as a word (\"students\") is a suffix, with a space before it. One chart has one unit, and mixing `$` and `%` is an inline error naming the first conflicting cell. A `%` in the data sets the units to `%` if none are given.\n- **Missing values:** blank, `—`, `n/a`. No bar is drawn, and a line shows a gap.\n- **Suppressed values:** the whole trimmed cell must match `*`, `<N`, `≤N`, or `<=N` (N a whole number).\n  - No mark is drawn.\n  - The data table keeps the original notation.\n  - \"Some values are suppressed for privacy\" appears once under the chart.\n- **Axes:** a bar chart always starts at zero. A line chart may start above zero and says so when it does. Values are labelled as typed, not re-rounded.\n- **Suggested type:** a long category label suggests horizontal bar but doesn't force it.\n- **Accessibility:** the SVG has `role=\"img\"` and the chart title as its accessible name. Under it, a `<details>` \"Show the data\" table is generated from the same data. The public site gets no JavaScript.\n- **Trusted SVG:** the chart block is replaced by a placeholder before nh3 runs, and the server-drawn SVG is swapped in after sanitizing. Every writer-typed string (title, labels, units, source, category and series names, cell text) is escaped before it goes into the SVG or the table. No uploaded SVG is ever served (ADR-004 unchanged).\n- **Builder (T17):** a dialog with a grid (categories down, series across) that accepts typing and an Excel or Sheets paste. It draws the chart live using the same server rendering, shows errors next to the cells, and has the Units field. In the body, a Chart is a card showing the drawn chart, with Edit and Remove.\n\n### Chart images in the Editor (T18)\n\n- \"Insert image\" lists the item's uploaded Chart images, and a description (alt) is required before inserting. It's stored as `![Description](image:<name>)` as today, and the existing upload, validation, and permissions (ADR-004) are unchanged.\n\n### Site preview (T12)\n\n- The draft is rendered through the public templates, `public_site.CSS`, and the site nav, with the item shown **as if published**: a draft Report appears in the nav. Other drafts stay hidden.\n- It's an embedded frame beside the Editor that drops below it on narrow screens, and it updates as the writer types (debounced, as today).\n- A Desktop/Phone width toggle.\n- \"Preview on site\" opens the same rendering in a new tab, showing the current **unsaved** edits (the form is posted to the tab, and nothing is saved).\n- A \"Draft preview, not published\" banner on every Site preview.\n- Preview routes require login and CSRF, save nothing, and follow the item's permissions (ADR-003).\n\n### Vocabulary\n\n- CONTEXT.md gains **Chart**, **Site preview**, and **Editor**, and **Chart image** is clarified as uploaded.\n- Avoid: graph, WYSIWYG, rich text, live view.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Behaviour is tested through `TestClient` with the `client` / `client_as(role)` fixtures, as in #1 and #11. The pure modules (HTML → Markdown conversion, chart parsing, SVG drawing) also get direct pytest tests.\n- **Round trip:**\n  - An untouched body posted back is stored byte-for-byte.\n  - A no-change round trip through the standard form renders equivalent HTML, for every seed body and every T09/T10 test fixture.\n  - An edit to one block changes only that block's rendered HTML.\n  - A locked block's bytes survive edits to the blocks around it.\n- **Sanitizing:** Editor HTML carrying `<script>`, `onerror=`, `style=`, `javascript:` hrefs, root-absolute hrefs, and unknown tags is stored as safe Markdown, with none of it surviving to any render.\n- **Links:**\n  - A `report:<id>` or `data-bite:<id>` link renders a correct relative href on the public page, in the export, and in the Site preview.\n  - A draft, unpublished, deleted, or unknown target renders plain text with no `<a>`.\n  - Publishing the target and re-running the export turns it into a link.\n- **Tables:** Excel-style HTML becomes a Markdown table. Numeric-column detection works across the formats listed above.\n- **Charts:**\n  - Parsing is tested for every numeric, missing, suppressed, currency, and unit-conflict case.\n  - The SVG is well-formed, escapes hostile titles, labels, and cells, and gives bar charts a zero baseline.\n  - \"Show the data\" preserves the original notation.\n  - The privacy note appears exactly once.\n  - Category limits are enforced.\n- **Site preview:** a draft's Site preview shows the banner and uses the public stylesheet. A draft Report appears in its own preview's nav but not in any other page or preview. Nothing is saved. Login and CSRF are required.\n- **Draft leak and export:** T08's crawl test still passes, with no draft content in `site/`, and the export is still identical to the live site.\n- **Browser behaviour** (toolbar, paste, the table controls, the chart dialog, the unsaved-changes warning) is checked by hand in Chrome and Safari, with screenshots in the ticket comment.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Pie, stacked, scatter, and dual-axis charts. Chart colour choice.\n- Autosave, revision history, and collaborative editing.\n- Uploading a pasted or dropped picture (it's refused, with a pointer to \"Insert image\").\n- A Markdown source toggle for writers.\n- Underline, fonts, colours, text alignment, code blocks, horizontal rules.\n- Embeds (Tableau Public, Power BI), which is ADR-004 unchanged.\n- Site preview of list pages (home, Data Bites index). The preview shows only the item's own page.\n- The admin console's visual design pass, which gets its own spec later.\n\n## Tickets\n\n- T12: Site preview\n- T13: Editor (ADR-005)\n- T14: Links to Reports and Data Bites\n- T15: Tables in the Editor\n- T16: Chart rendering (ADR-006)\n- T17: Chart builder\n- T18: Chart images in the Editor\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"468a1b0e-a905-41c5-a26f-79ba3f74ec53","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"ff3a26f0-942e-45da-9d40-7cb33109e6ba","isSidechain":false,"type":"system","subtype":"away_summary","content":"You're making the CMS usable without Markdown: a visual editor, table and chart builders, and a preview that looks like the public site. The spec draft is written but not on GitHub yet; once you approve it, I'll create the spec issue. (disable recaps in /config)","timestamp":"2026-09-30T19:24:55.862Z","uuid":"c18e993c-28c9-4f59-9d72-0c6d108aba70","isMeta":false,"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"c18e993c-28c9-4f59-9d72-0c6d108aba70","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"093450ba-ec73-4db7-9f50-dd34721d4f53","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"\n\n<pasted_content id=\"7025\">\n> The six points you called out are approved, subject to the corrections below.\n>\n> 1. **Internal-link IDs are not currently stable after deletion.** Both tables use `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`, and the code explicitly notes that SQLite may reuse the highest deleted ID. A deleted `report:7` could later point to an unrelated new Report numbered 7. T14 must define how IDs are made permanently non-reusable or introduce a separate immutable reference key. It must also explain how the Editor distinguishes “Item deleted” from an ID that never existed.\n> 2. **Locked-block preservation needs an explicit mechanism.** Rendering Markdown to sanitized HTML loses the original bytes of raw HTML, code fences, and unsupported headings. Before rendering Editor HTML, extract unsupported source blocks and replace them with opaque locked-block tokens. On save, restore the original fragments from the stored database body, not from client-supplied hidden content. Reject unknown or duplicated tokens.\n> 3. **Define the fenced Chart format.** Specify a versioned grammar, preferably a fenced `chart` block containing strict JSON parsed with the standard library. Define required keys, allowed keys, types, limits, malformed-block behavior, and canonical serialization. A malformed block submitted through the Markdown fallback must render inertly or be rejected, never bypass validation.\n> 4. **Strengthen the trusted-SVG boundary.** The placeholder approach is acceptable, but SVG inserted after nh3 receives no further sanitization. The implementation must:\n>    - use collision-resistant server-generated placeholders;\n>    - validate all chart fields before rendering;\n>    - reject non-finite values such as `NaN` and infinity;\n>    - generate only a fixed allowlist of SVG elements and attributes;\n>    - escape every writer-controlled string in both SVG and the data table;\n>    - never copy writer-provided markup, attributes, URLs, IDs, or CSS into the SVG.\n>\n>    Tests should inspect the generated element and attribute set, not only try several hostile strings.\n> 5. **Reconcile external links with the relative-path rule.** I approve rejecting `http:` and allowing only `https:` and `mailto:` externally. Update the documented hard rule to say that all **site-owned** links and assets use relative paths, while explicit external links may use `https:` or `mailto:`. The current T07/T08 crawler rejects every URL containing `://`, so it must skip approved external links while continuing to reject root-absolute internal paths and verify every internal link.\n> 6. **Browser checks are approved**, but screenshots are evidence, not the test themselves. Each ticket comment should record the browser/version, viewport, actions performed, and observed result alongside the screenshots.\n>\n> The expanded round-trip fixtures and item-page-only Site preview scope are approved.\n>\n> Revise the spec with these points and show me the changed sections before creating the GitHub issue or committing `CONTEXT.md`.\n</pasted_content id=\"7025\">\n"},"uuid":"c35578e2-559d-4776-8e5e-1289e9a05dfe","timestamp":"2026-09-30T19:25:46.314Z","permissionMode":"auto","origin":{"kind":"human"},"promptSource":"typed","turnOrigin":"human","turnPosition":{"promptIndex":6,"turnIndex":6},"userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"8958b5ed-dd87-438f-9932-43d3a378768b","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaB3k4a1GZPDNd4UPP56","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01CbQCi2J8CYSzRd9LYu69ut","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc/scratchpad/spec-editor.md","old_string":"- **Untouched is byte-for-byte:** if the writer changes nothing, the stored Markdown is kept exactly, and opening the Editor never rewrites it.\n- **An edited body is saved in standard Markdown form:** any body the Editor has changed is rewritten in one standard form.\n- **Locked blocks:** a block the Editor can't represent (code block, raw HTML, H4 or deeper, etc.) shows as a read-only block reading \"This part can't be edited here\". Its original Markdown is kept byte-for-byte even when blocks around it are edited. No current content triggers this.","new_string":"- **Base version:** the edit form carries a hash of the stored body as the Editor loaded it (`body_base`). On save, if the stored body's hash no longer matches (someone else saved in between), the save is refused with \"This item changed since you opened it. Reload to see the latest version.\" Nothing is merged.\n- **Untouched is byte-for-byte:** the Editor posts `body_dirty=0` until the writer's first change. With `body_dirty=0` and a matching `body_base`, the server keeps the stored body exactly and ignores the posted HTML. The client can only choose \"keep what is stored\", so trusting the flag grants nothing. Opening the Editor never rewrites the body.\n- **An edited body is saved in standard Markdown form:** any body the Editor has changed is rewritten in one standard form.\n- **Locked blocks:** a top-level block the Editor can't represent shows as a read-only block reading \"This part can't be edited here\" (with a Remove button), and its original bytes are kept even when blocks around it are edited. No current content triggers this. The mechanism:\n  - **Detection:** the stored body is parsed with markdown-it. A top-level block is *supported* only if it and everything inside it is in the Editor's set: paragraph, H2, H3, bulleted and numbered list, block quote, table, a valid `chart` fence, and inline bold, italic, line break, links allowed under T14, and `image:<name>` images. Anything else locks the whole top-level block it sits in, e.g. a code block, raw HTML, H1 or H4 and deeper, a horizontal rule, or an inline code span in a paragraph. Its exact source bytes come from the token's line map.\n  - **Before rendering Editor HTML:** each locked block is cut out of the source and replaced by an opaque token (`locked-<n>`, n being its position among the stored body's locked blocks). {"parentUuid":"9eb16331-93cc-4f68-9f80-de8bc98cbe8a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaB3k4a1GZPDNd4UPP56","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_018MRah9nWf6oKx5rrke65M6","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc/scratchpad/spec-editor.md","old_string":"- External links are limited to `https:` and `mailto:`. Anything else, including `javascript:`, root-absolute `/…`, and `http:`, is refused with a message in the link dialog and removed by the server on save.\n- **Links within the site** are stored as `report:<id>` or `data-bite:<id>`, by the stable database id and never by title or slug. The Markdown pipeline resolves them at render time to the page-relative path, like `image:<name>` (ADR-004).\n- A target that's a draft, unpublished, deleted, or missing renders as **plain text** (its link text, with no `<a>`), never as an empty or unsafe link. The reference stays stored, so it becomes a link again if the target is published.\n- In the Editor, such links are marked \"Not published: will show as plain text\" or \"Item deleted\".\n- Deleting an item shows the items whose bodies link to it, and the delete isn't blocked.\n- `cms publish` regenerates all of `site/` on every run (`app/publish.py`), so a link becomes live on the first publish after its target is published. No pages need rebuilding individually.","new_string":"- **The rule, restated:** every *site-owned* link and asset uses a relative path. Only an *explicit external link* (`<a href>`) may be absolute, and only as `https:` or `mailto:`. The Editor's link dialog refuses anything else (`http:`, `javascript:`, root-absolute `/…`, other schemes) with a message.\n- **The link pipeline enforces it for every body, however it was saved:** at render time, an `<a>` keeps its href only if the href is `https:`, `mailto:`, or a site reference (below) that resolves. Anything else renders as its link text with no `<a>`. This covers the Markdown fallback and any stored content, not only the Editor.\n- **Stable references, not ids:** SQLite may reuse the highest deleted `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (noted in `app/data_bites.py` and `app/reports.py`), so the id isn't safe to link by.\n  - Each Data Bite and Report gets an immutable `ref` column: 16 lowercase hex characters from `secrets.token_hex(8)`, set at creation, never edited, never reused.\n  - It's added through `ADDED_COLUMNS`, with existing rows given refs by `init_db`, plus `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` on each table.\n  - A site link is stored as `report:<ref>` or `data-bite:<ref>` and resolved at render time to the page-relative path, like `image:<name>` (ADR-004). Never by title, slug, or id.\n- **Deleted versus never existed:** deleting a Data Bite or Report writes a tombstone row `deleted_refs(kind, ref, deleted_at)` in the same transaction. A ref found in its table is a live or draft item. A ref found only in `deleted_refs` was deleted. A ref in neither never existed (e.g. typed by hand in the fallback).\n- **Unresolvable targets:** a draft, unpublished, deleted, or never-existing target renders as **plain text** (its link text, with no `<a>`), never as an empty or unsafe link. The reference stays stored, so it becomes a link again if its target is published.\n- In the Editor, such links are marked \"Not published: will show as plain text\", \"Item deleted\", or \"Unknown link\".\n- Deleting an item shows the items whose bodies link to it, and the delete isn't blocked.\n- `cms publish` regenerates all of `site/` on every run (`app/publish.py`), so a link becomes live on the first publish after its target is published. No pages need rebuilding individually.\n- **Docs and crawler change together in T14:**\n  - The CLAUDE.md hard rule becomes \"Site-owned links and assets use **relative** paths only. Never `href=\"/...\"` or `src=\"/...\"`. Explicit external links may use `https:` or `mailto:`.\" ADR-001 gets a matching note.\n  - The T07/T08 crawler skips an `<a href>` that is `https:` or `mailto:`. It still fails on any root-absolute path, any other `://` URL, and any `src` that isn't relative, and it still fetches and checks every internal link."},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5362,"cache_read_input_tokens":91819,"output_tokens":5465,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":382},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5362,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":5465,"cache_read_input_tokens":91819,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5362,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5362},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_018MRah9nWf6oKx5rrke65M6":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc/scratchpad/spec-editor.md","old_string":"- External links are limited to `https:` and `mailto:`. {"parentUuid":"35e0cc7c-3bb1-446a-addf-c31388a0cd0f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaB3k4a1GZPDNd4UPP56","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01UBkskFzeJ7Tv4tTZdGBAUk","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc/scratchpad/spec-editor.md","old_string":"- **Stored** as a fenced `chart` block in the Markdown body, holding the type, title, axis labels, units, source, and data. Writers never see it.\n- **Types:** vertical bar, horizontal bar, line. 1 to 4 series, with a legend when there's more than one. Up to 30 categories for bar charts and 60 for line charts.\n- **Fields:** title (required), x- and y-axis labels (optional), Units (optional), Source/note (optional; one line of plain text with no formatting).","new_string":"- **Stored** as a fenced block whose info string is exactly `chart`, containing one strict JSON object parsed with stdlib `json`. Writers never see it.\n- **Grammar, version 1:**\n\n  | Key | Required | Type and limits |\n  |---|---|---|\n  | `version` | yes | the integer `1` |\n  | `type` | yes | `\"bar\"`, `\"hbar\"`, or `\"line\"` |\n  | `title` | yes | string, 1 to 120 characters |\n  | `x_label`, `y_label` | no | string, up to 60 characters |\n  | `unit` | no | `{\"text\": string of 1 to 20 characters, \"position\": \"prefix\" or \"suffix\"}` |\n  | `source` | no | string, up to 200 characters |\n  | `categories` | yes | array of 1 to 30 strings for `bar`/`hbar`, or 2 to 60 for `line`; each 1 to 60 characters; no duplicates |\n  | `series` | yes | array of 1 to 4 `{\"name\": string of 1 to 40 characters, \"values\": [...]}`, with names unique and `values` exactly as long as `categories` |\n  | `values[i]` | yes | string, up to 20 characters: the cell **as typed**, parsed at render by the number rules below, so \"as typed\" labels and suppressed notation survive |\n\n  - Every string must be single-line (no control characters, including newlines and tabs) and is Unicode NFC-normalized on save.\n  - Unknown keys, missing required keys, wrong types, duplicate JSON keys (checked with `object_pairs_hook`), `NaN`, `Infinity`, trailing data, and any block over 32 KB make the block **invalid**.\n  - A value cell that fails the number rules is also invalid, unless it's a missing or suppressed value.\n- **Canonical serialization:** keys in the table's order, absent optional keys omitted, `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)`, and a trailing newline inside the fence. The Editor and the fallback both save this form.\n- **Malformed blocks:** validation runs on **every save path**, the Editor and the Markdown fallback alike. A body containing an invalid `chart` block is refused with a form error that names the problem, e.g. \"Chart 2: series 'Fall 2025' has 29 values but 30 categories\". As defense in depth, rendering an invalid block (such as stored content validated under older rules) outputs the fixed text \"This chart could not be shown.\" and nothing else, from no writer-controlled input.\n- **Types:** vertical bar, horizontal bar, line. 1 to 4 series, with a legend when there's more than one. Up to 30 categories for bar charts and 60 for line charts.\n- **Fields:** title (required), x- and y-axis labels (optional), Units (optional; one field in the builder, stored with its prefix or suffix position), Source/note (optional; one line of plain text with no formatting)."},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5362,"cache_read_input_tokens":91819,"output_tokens":5465,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":382},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5362,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":5465,"cache_read_input_tokens":91819,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5362,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5362},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01UBkskFzeJ7Tv4tTZdGBAUk":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc/scratchpad/spec-editor.md","old_string":"- **Stored** as a fenced `chart` block in the Markdown body, holding the type, title, axis labels, units, source, and data. Writers never see it.\n- **Types:** vertical bar, horizontal bar, line. 1 to 4 series, with a legend when there's more than one. Up to 30 categories for bar charts and 60 for line charts.\n- **Fields:** title (required), x- and y-axis labels (optional), Units (optional), Source/note (optional; one line of plain text with no formatting).","newString":"- **Stored** as a fenced block whose info string is exactly `chart`, containing one strict JSON object parsed with stdlib `json`. Writers never see it.\n- **Grammar, version 1:**\n\n  | Key | Required | Type and limits |\n  |---|---|---|\n  | `version` | yes | the integer `1` |\n  | `type` | yes | `\"bar\"`, `\"hbar\"`, or `\"line\"` |\n  | `title` | yes | string, 1 to 120 characters |\n  | `x_label`, `y_label` | no | string, up to 60 characters |\n  | `unit` | no | `{\"text\": string of 1 to 20 characters, \"position\": \"prefix\" or \"suffix\"}` |\n  | `source` | no | string, up to 200 characters |\n  | `categories` | yes | array of 1 to 30 strings for `bar`/`hbar`, or 2 to 60 for `line`; each 1 to 60 characters; no duplicates |\n  | `series` | yes | array of 1 to 4 `{\"name\": string of 1 to 40 characters, \"values\": [...]}`, with names unique and `values` exactly as long as `categories` |\n  | `values[i]` | yes | string, up to 20 characters: the cell **as typed**, parsed at render by the number rules below, so \"as typed\" labels and suppressed notation survive |\n\n  - Every string must be single-line (no control characters, including newlines and tabs) and is Unicode NFC-normalized on save.\n  - Unknown keys, missing required keys, wrong types, duplicate JSON keys (checked with `object_pairs_hook`), `NaN`, `Infinity`, trailing data, and any block over 32 KB make the block **invalid**.\n  - A value cell that fails the number rules is also invalid, unless it's a missing or suppressed value.\n- **Canonical serialization:** keys in the table's order, absent optional keys omitted, `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)`, and a trailing newline inside the fence. The Editor and the fallback both save this form.\n- **Malformed blocks:** validation runs on **every save path**, the Editor and the Markdown fallback alike. A body containing an invalid `chart` block is refused with a form error that names the problem, e.g. \"Chart 2: series 'Fall 2025' has 29 values but 30 categories\". As defense in depth, rendering an invalid block (such as stored content validated under older rules) outputs the fixed text \"This chart could not be shown.\" and nothing else, from no writer-controlled input.\n- **Types:** vertical bar, horizontal bar, line. 1 to 4 series, with a legend when there's more than one. The public site gets no JavaScript.","-- **Trusted SVG:** the chart block is replaced by a placeholder before nh3 runs, and the server-drawn SVG is swapped in after sanitizing. Every writer-typed string (title, labels, units, source, category and series names, cell text) is escaped before it goes into the SVG or the table. No uploaded SVG is ever served (ADR-004 unchanged).","+- **Trusted SVG boundary:** nothing inserted after nh3 is sanitized again, so the chart's HTML must be safe because of how it's built, not by filtering.","+  - **Placeholders:** each render generates a fresh `secrets.token_hex(16)` nonce *after* the writer's input is fixed. Each valid chart fence renders as the placeholder `chart-<nonce>-<n>`. After nh3, each placeholder must occur exactly once and is replaced exactly once. A missing, extra, or leftover placeholder fails the render loudly (an exception, and a 500 in the admin console) rather than emitting anything partial.","+  - **Validate first:** a chart is drawn only from a block that passed the full grammar above. Values are parsed to Python `float`s and checked with `math.isfinite`, and anything non-finite is rejected before drawing.","+  - **Fixed vocabulary:** the renderer emits only these elements: `figure`, `figcaption`, `svg`, `g`, `title`, `rect`, `line`, `polyline`, `circle`, `text`, `p`, `small`, `details`, `summary`, `table`, `thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th`, `td`. It emits only these attributes: `class`, `viewBox`, `role`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-hidden`, `id`, `x`, `y`, `x1`, `y1`, `x2`, `y2`, `width`, `height`, `cx`, `cy`, `r`, `points`, `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `text-anchor`, `scope`.","+  - **Attribute values:**","+    - Numbers are formatted by the renderer.","+    - `fill` and `stroke` come only from the fixed palette constants.","+    - `class` comes only from fixed class names.","+    - `id` is only `chart-<nonce>-<n>-title`.","+    - There's never an `href`, `style`, `on*`, or URL-bearing attribute.","+  - **Writer text:** every writer-controlled string (title, labels, unit, source, category and series names, cell text) appears only as escaped *text content* (`html.escape`), in both the SVG and the data table. Never as an attribute value, element name, id, class, URL, or CSS.","+  - No uploaded SVG is ever served (ADR-004 unchanged)."," - **Builder (T17):** a dialog with a grid (categories down, series across) that accepts typing and an Excel or Sheets paste. It draws the chart live using the same server rendering, shows errors next to the cells, and has the Units field. In the body, a Chart is a card showing the drawn chart, with Edit and Remove."," "," ### Chart images in the Editor (T18)"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b2e23642-39d4-43cf-973a-9e47e3d0561a","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

Publishing the target and re-running the export turns it into a link.","new_string":"- **Links:**\n  - A `report:<ref>` or `data-bite:<ref>` link renders a correct relative href on the public page, in the export, and in the Site preview, at every page depth.\n  - Canonical serialization is stable (saving it again changes nothing).\n  - Parsing is tested for every numeric, missing, suppressed, currency, and unit-conflict case.\n  - **Structural allowlist test:** for a set of charts (every type, 1 and 4 series, negatives, missing and suppressed cells, all optional fields), the rendered figure is parsed with `html.parser`. The test collects every element name and every attribute name and asserts both sets are subsets of the fixed vocabulary. It asserts every `fill`/`stroke` is a palette constant, every `class` is a fixed name, and every `id` matches `chart-<nonce>-<n>-title`, with no `href`, `style`, or `on*` anywhere.\n  - Hostile writer strings (`<script>`, `\"><svg onload=…>`, `javascript:`, `</title>`, `&`) in every text field appear only as escaped text content, which the same parse confirms.\n  - Placeholders: a writer who types the placeholder shape into the body gets it rendered as inert text. Two charts get distinct placeholders.\n  - An invalid block reaching render outputs only the fixed \"could not be shown\" text.\n  - Bar charts have a zero baseline. \"Show the data\" preserves the original notation. The privacy note appears exactly once."},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":6011,"cache_read_input_tokens":97181,"output_tokens":2243,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":73},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":6011,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2243,"cache_read_input_tokens":97181,"cache_creation_input_tokens":6011,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":6011},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01V8V5SHGGLAakBRRm1HBjdb":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc/scratchpad/spec-editor.md","old_string":"- **Charts:**\n  - Parsing is tested for every numeric, missing, suppressed, currency, and unit-conflict case.\n  - The SVG is well-formed, escapes hostile titles, labels, and cells, and gives bar charts a zero baseline.\n  - \"Show the data\" preserves the original notation.\n  - The privacy note appears exactly once.\n  - Category limits are enforced.","new_string":"- **Charts:**\n  - Grammar: every required key missing, every unknown key, every wrong type, duplicate keys, `NaN`/`Infinity`, over-long strings, newlines in strings, mismatched `values` lengths, too many categories or series, and a block over 32 KB are each rejected, **on both the Editor and the Markdown fallback save paths**. {"parentUuid":"bdbc56df-73d1-4cbc-a25b-08e63c20790c","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfaB8uefTcm5uRMWLeEYi","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The spec revision is done. Below are the sections that changed. The full file is at `…/scratchpad/spec-editor.md`, and nothing has been created on GitHub or committed yet.\n\n### Editor → Locked blocks and base version (correction 2)\n- **Base version:** the form carries `body_base`, a hash of the stored body when the Editor loaded it. If someone else saved in the meantime, the save is refused with \"This item changed since you opened it. Reload…\". Nothing is merged.\n- **Untouched:** the Editor posts `body_dirty=0` until the first change. With a matching `body_base`, the server keeps the stored body exactly and ignores the posted HTML. The flag can only choose \"keep what's stored\", so trusting it grants nothing.\n- **Detection:** markdown-it parses the stored body. A top-level block is supported only if everything in it is in the Editor's set: paragraph, H2 and H3, lists, block quote, table, a valid `chart` fence, and inline bold, italic, line break, allowed links, and `image:<name>`.\n  - Anything else (code block, raw HTML, H1, H4 or deeper, a horizontal rule, an inline code span) locks the whole top-level block it's in.\n  - The exact bytes come from the token's line map.\n- **Before rendering:** locked blocks are cut out and replaced by `locked-<n>` tokens. Their source never reaches the browser as data. They're shown read-only, with a Remove button.\n- **On save:** each token is restored from the **stored database body**, never from anything the client sent. An unknown or duplicated token refuses the save. A missing token means the writer removed that block.\n\n### Links (corrections 1 and 5)\n- **Rule restated:** site-owned links and assets are relative. Only an explicit `<a href>` may be absolute, and only as `https:` or `mailto:`.\n- **Enforced when rendering every body:** an `<a>` keeps its href only if it's `https:`, `mailto:`, or a site reference that resolves. Anything else renders as plain link text. This covers the Markdown fallback too.\n- **Stable references:**\n  - A new immutable `ref` column on both tables, from `secrets.token_hex(8)`, added through `ADDED_COLUMNS`.\n  - `init_db` gives existing rows a ref, and a `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` enforces uniqueness.\n  - Links are stored as `report:<ref>` or `data-bite:<ref>`, never by id, slug or title.\n- **Deleted vs. never existed:** deleting an item writes a tombstone to `deleted_refs(kind, ref, deleted_at)` in the same transaction.\n  - A ref in its table is a live item or a draft.\n  - A ref only in `deleted_refs` shows \"Item deleted\".\n  - A ref in neither shows \"Unknown link\".\n- **Docs and crawler change together in T14:**\n  - The CLAUDE.md hard rule gets the wording you gave, and ADR-001 gets a matching note.\n  - The crawler skips `https:` and `mailto:` `<a href>`s.\n  - It still fails on a root-absolute path, any other `://`, and any `src` that isn't relative, and it still checks every internal link.\n\n### Charts: format (correction 3)\n- A fenced block with info string `chart` holds one strict JSON object, parsed with stdlib `json`, version `1`. The keys:\n  - `version`, `type` (`bar`/`hbar`/`line`) and `title` (1–120 characters)\n  - optional `x_label` and `y_label` (≤60), `unit` `{text ≤20, position prefix|suffix}` and `source` (≤200)\n  - `categories`: 1–30 for bar charts, 2–60 for line charts, each ≤60 characters, no duplicates\n  - `series`: 1–4 entries, each with a `name` (≤40, unique) and `values` of the same length as `categories`\n  - each value is the cell **as typed** (≤20 characters)\n- **Strings:** single-line, with no control characters, normalized to NFC.\n- **Invalid:** unknown or missing keys, wrong types, duplicate keys (checked with `object_pairs_hook`), `NaN` or `Infinity`, trailing data, anything over 32 KB, or an unparseable cell.\n- **Canonical form:** keys in the fixed order, `ensure_ascii=False, indent=2`, and a trailing newline.\n- **Malformed blocks:** checked on **every save path**. The Editor and the fallback both refuse with a named error (e.g. \"Chart 2: series 'Fall 2025' has 29 values but 30 categories\"). If one ever reaches rendering, it outputs only the fixed text \"This chart could not be shown.\"\n\n### Charts: trusted SVG (correction 4)\n- **Placeholder:** `chart-<nonce>-<n>`, with the nonce from `secrets.token_hex(16)` and generated per render, after the input is fixed. Each placeholder must appear exactly once after nh3, or the render fails loudly (a 500, never partial output).\n- **Validated first:** every value is a `float` checked with `math.isfinite`.\n- **Fixed elements and attributes:** only the elements and attributes listed in the spec are emitted.\n  - `fill` and `stroke` come only from palette constants, and `class` only from fixed names.\n  - `id` is only `chart-<nonce>-<n>-title`.\n  - There's never an `href`, `style`, `on*` or URL-bearing attribute.\n- **Writer text:** it appears only as `html.escape`d text content, never in an attribute, id, class, URL or CSS.\n\n### Testing (all six corrections)\n- **Round trip:**\n  - The Editor HTML never contains a locked block's source bytes.\n  - Unknown, duplicated or forged tokens are refused, and removing a token drops only that block.\n  - A stale `body_base` is refused.\n  - With `body_dirty=0`, the stored body is kept even when the posted HTML differs.\n- **Links:**\n  - **The id-reuse test:** delete a link's target, create a new Report that may take the old id, and the link is still plain text marked \"Item deleted\".\n  - Refs are backfilled, unique, and survive changes to title and slug.\n  - Hostile or relative hrefs from the fallback render as plain text.\n  - A test injects a bad URL to prove the crawler still catches it.\n- **Charts:**\n  - Every grammar violation is rejected on **both** save paths, and saving the canonical form again changes nothing.\n  - **The allowlist test:** it parses the rendered figure with `html.parser`, collects every element and attribute name, and checks them against the fixed vocabulary, along with the palette, class and id patterns.\n  - Hostile strings are confirmed to be escaped text only.\n  - A placeholder typed into the body stays inert, and two charts get distinct placeholders.\n- **Browser checks:** each check records the browser and exact version, viewport, step-by-step actions, observed result with pass or fail, and screenshots as supporting evidence. They add to pytest and never replace it.\n\n### Two behaviour changes these corrections cause, which need your decision\n1. **External `https:` images.** `tests/test_t10_chart_images.py:345` currently allows `![Logo](https://example.test/logo.png)` through the Markdown fallback. An image isn't an explicit link, so under the restated rule it's no longer allowed. I recommend it renders nothing, and I'd update that T10 test. It's also the same draft-gate gap ADR-004 was written to close.\n2. **Relative links typed by hand** (e.g. `[CDS](reports/cds.html)` in the fallback) now render as plain text, because only `https:`, `mailto:` and resolved site references survive. I recommend accepting this, since a relative path typed by hand breaks depending on the page's depth.\n\nIf you approve these two, I'll create the spec issue and commit `CONTEXT.md`."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2819,"cache_read_input_tokens":103192,"output_tokens":3089,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":425},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2819,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":3089,"cache_read_input_tokens":103192,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2819,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2819},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"328605d3-f645-420d-adef-af4a80a7a0b5","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CfaB8uAQj7uzKyvdU2VjG","type":"assistant","uuid":"780ddff7-8c98-4607-bf35-64a61f1d8e3c","timestamp":"2026-09-30T19:28:24.594Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

It belongs to its item and is published with\nit (ADR-004). Not a **Chart**, which the CMS draws from data, and not a\nReport's **attached file**, which is a PDF offered for download.\n_Avoid_: figure, graphic, media, attachment\n\n**Chart**:\nA bar, horizontal bar, or line chart the CMS *draws* from data typed or\npasted into it, shown inline in a Data Bite or Report body with its data\navailable as a table (spec #14). Stored in the body as a `chart` block the\nwriter never sees. Not a **Chart image**, which is made elsewhere and uploaded.\n_Avoid_: graph, plot, visualization\n\n**Editor**:\nThe visual body editor on a Data Bite's or Report's edit page: a toolbar,\ntables edited in place, Charts, and Chart images, with no Markdown in sight.\nThe body is still stored as Markdown (spec #14).\n_Avoid_: WYSIWYG, rich text, rich-text editor\n\n**Site preview**:\nA Draft (or unsaved edits) rendered as its public page would look, with the\nsite's nav and stylesheet and a \"Draft preview, not published\" banner. Saves\nnothing and publishes nothing.\n_Avoid_: live view, public preview"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":325,"cache_read_input_tokens":113001,"output_tokens":997,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":202},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":325,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":997,"cache_read_input_tokens":113001,"cache_creation_input_tokens":325,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":325},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01AZQMzywaLZwUMjJKPNHdCG":{"file_path":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","old_string":"**Chart image**:\nA PNG, JPEG, or WebP picture (usually a graph made in Excel, R, or Tableau)\nthat a Data Bite or Report shows inline, placed in its Markdown body as\n`image:<name>`.
